candidates.next_evidence: Track 2026 capex split, CoWoS/SoIC capacity additions, advanced-node utilization, customer prepayments, and whether packaging capacity remains the binding constraint versus wafer capacity.
candidates.node_relation: Primary capacity owner for leading-edge logic nodes and advanced packaging technologies including CoWoS, InFO, SoIC and related 2.5D/3D integration.
candidates.theme_relation: AI accelerators and custom ASICs require leading-edge process technology plus advanced packaging to integrate logic, HBM, interposers and substrates.
candidates.why_include: TSMC is a direct chokepoint candidate because AI chip output can be constrained by both wafer starts at advanced nodes and advanced packaging capacity. Its 2025 annual-report language explicitly ties leading-edge, specialty and advanced-packaging investment to customer growth and AI demand.

candidates.next_evidence: Track EUV and High-NA EUV bookings, backlog, shipment timing, export-control impacts, customer concentration, and whether memory/HBM demand competes with logic for tool slots.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier of EUV lithography systems required for leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing; lithography tool supply and service capacity can constrain advanced-node ramps.
candidates.theme_relation: AI logic and advanced memory demand drives leading-edge fab investment, which depends on EUV tool availability, installation, service and customer acceptance.
candidates.why_include: ASML is one of the clearest scarce-supplier mappings in this node because EUV lithography has very limited supplier diversity and is tied directly to leading-edge capacity expansion.

candidates.next_evidence: Separate AI-driven order contribution from broader WFE cyclicality; check segment disclosures, advanced-packaging tool traction, backlog durability, and exposure to China export controls.
candidates.node_relation: Broad wafer-fab equipment supplier with exposure to leading-edge logic, high-bandwidth memory, deposition/materials engineering, and advanced packaging process steps.
candidates.theme_relation: AI compute growth increases demand for GAA logic, HBM and advanced packaging, which raises process complexity and equipment intensity.
candidates.why_include: Applied Materials has a direct equipment-vendor relation to multiple AI semiconductor capacity constraints. Its 2025 product release specifically targeted leading-edge GAA logic, HBM DRAM and advanced packaging for AI chips.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify advanced-packaging revenue scale versus total revenue, customer concentration, HBM-linked demand, backlog, and whether growth is tool-share gain or cyclical WFE recovery.
candidates.node_relation: Supplier of etch/deposition and advanced-packaging equipment used in interconnects, memory, wafer-level and panel-level packaging processes.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Semiconductor etch, deposition and packaging equipment
candidates.theme_relation: AI accelerators and HBM increase device complexity, packaging density and process steps, supporting demand for specialized process equipment.
candidates.why_include: Lam is a plausible chokepoint supplier because its advanced-packaging portfolio addresses larger AI packages and high-performance computing interconnect scaling, while its core etch/deposition franchises are critical to advanced semiconductor manufacturing.

candidates.next_evidence: Quantify AI supply-chain revenue exposure, advanced-packaging order backlog, HBM customer wins, competitive position versus KLA/Camtek, and whether revenue depends on a small number of OSAT or memory customers.
candidates.node_relation: Metrology and inspection supplier with advanced-packaging and advanced-node exposure; process-control intensity rises as packaging architectures and feature sizes become more complex.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Semiconductor metrology, inspection and process-control equipment
candidates.theme_relation: AI-driven multi-die packages, HBM integration and advanced nodes require tighter overlay, inspection, metrology and yield-management capabilities.
candidates.why_include: Onto is a less obvious US-listed equipment candidate. Its annual-report materials state that AI applications have generated significant demand and new technology requirements in advanced packaging, and its product set maps to metrology/inspection bottlenecks rather than headline lithography.

evidence.claim: TSMC's 2025 annual-report materials state that it is developing advanced packaging and 3D chip-stacking technologies including CoWoS, InFO and SoIC, and investing in leading-edge, specialty and advanced-packaging technologies to support customer growth; the report also links demand strength to AI.
ASML's 2025 annual-report materials identify EUV lithography systems as core products and discuss semiconductor demand connected to AI logic and memory products.
ASML reported Q2 2025 net bookings of EUR 5.5 billion, including EUR 2.3 billion EUV, and management said AI customer fundamentals remained strong looking into 2026.
evidence.source_title: ASML reports €7.7 billion total net sales and €2.3 billion net income in Q2 2025

evidence.claim: Applied Materials introduced chipmaking products in 2025 targeting leading-edge GAA logic, HBM DRAM and advanced packaging, describing these as critical areas for more powerful AI chips.
evidence.source_title: Applied Materials Unveils Next-Gen Chipmaking Products to Supercharge AI Performance

evidence.claim: Lam Research describes its advanced-packaging portfolio as addressing large-format package interconnect needs for larger AI packages across wafer and panel platforms for high-performance computing.

Onto Innovation's annual-report materials describe advanced packaging as wafer- or panel-level technologies and state that AI applications have generated significant demand and new technology requirements in advanced packaging.

Amkor remains a relevant watchlist extension outside the five-candidate limit: it is a US-listed OSAT building advanced-packaging capacity in Arizona, with production expected in 2028 according to current reporting.

memory_update.text: Core US-listed/ADR names for advanced foundry, packaging and lithography chokepoint: TSM, ASML, AMAT, LRCX, ONTO. KLA and AMKR should remain next-pass candidates if the dashboard allows more than five.

The node has at least four separable bottleneck layers: leading-edge wafer capacity, EUV lithography tool availability, advanced-packaging process equipment/metrology, and OSAT/package assembly capacity.

Need a separate pass on substrate/interposer suppliers and non-US-listed but US-accessible ADRs/OTC names such as ASE Technology, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron and substrate materials vendors; many key bottleneck suppliers may not be standard US exchange listings.

Need to verify whether KLA should replace or join ONTO in the final universe; KLA has strong process-control relevance and official FY2025 materials mention AI infrastructure and advanced packaging growth.

node: Leading-edge foundry, advanced packaging, and lithography
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI advanced foundry/packaging/lithography chokepoint. The highest-relevance names cluster around: leading-edge wafer capacity, EUV lithography, wafer-fab equipment for GAA/HBM/advanced packaging, advanced-packaging process tools, and outsourced advanced packaging/test capacity. This is research mapping only, not a trading recommendation.
